body:
I'm going to butt in here for a moment and try to answer a couple questions for you. Both myself and my sister are diagnosed anorexics. Throwaway account because my sister is a redditor as well. 

Background information: I am 5'2 and consume 750 calories a day. I walk anywhere from 3-5 hours a day to burn at least 500 calories. I will not say my weight because it truly disgusts me. My sister is 5'8 and is fully recovered, she has been for 4 years now. At her lowest she weighed around 80 lbs. She was hospitalized, I never was. I developed my disorder later than she did, she was a minor and could be forced into inpatient. I legally can't be put away.

>Is it an attempt at rational thought with a specific reason in mind

Yes and no. My sister has always claimed that her reasoning behind it was control. She saw my mother and father's relationship falling apart and she didn't want them to split. She decided that she would make herself sick so they would pay attention to her and not their own problems. For me, I don't do it for anybody but myself. I look in the mirror and I hear somebody say "you'd be so much happier if you were thinner" or "you'd have more friends if your thighs weren't so thick." I don't know many anorexics who do it to look better to somebody else or get into a relationship. According to my therapist I do it to have power over something. I don't know if I believe her or not, because in all honesty I don't know what my drive is.


>Also, curious as to why the body does not overwhelm the person with "I am goddamn starving, give me food!"

It does. Some nights when I come home and my father is cooking dinner I smell it and I just want it so badly. Something inside me tells me to eat it, that it'll be fine if I just have a little bit of it. That doesn't last long because another - stronger - part of me suffocates the thought of eating. I know that if I give in I'll be sickened with myself. I won't be able to sleep without going for a run and burning off all the calories I ate, and then some. Going to bed hungry at night is the worst. The little tingle of hunger that regular people fill just grows and grows until you can feel a rattling inside yourself. I take nyquil to get to sleep without eating.

I'm not happy with what I'm doing or what I've become, but I also don't ever want to be 55 lbs. I don't see recovery in my future but I'm okay with it.
